idea-plugin.name: Scope Tracer
idea-plugin.description:
Shows how Java structured concurrency (java.util.concurrent.StructuredTaskScope) actually ran: the tree of scopes and forked tasks, how long each task lived, which one failed and which siblings were cancelled. It reads JFR recordings made by scope-tracer.

Two actions in the Tools menu:

  • Run with Scope Tracer runs the selected Java application or JUnit run configuration with the scope-tracer agent, --enable-preview and a JFR recording, and opens the trace in the Scope Tracer tool window when the run ends: one trace per JVM, so tests that fork JVMs give one tab each. For tests it is also in the run gutter icon's menu and the editor's context menu.
  • Open .jfr Recording (Scope Tracer)... opens a recording you made elsewhere in the same tool window. Clicking a task jumps to the fork call that created it.

Requirements: IntelliJ IDEA 2026.3 or later. A JDK 27 must be installed: traced runs need a JDK 27 in the run configuration, and the bundled analyzer runs as a separate process on a JDK 27 or newer, found among the IDE's JDKs or chosen in Settings | Tools | Scope Tracer.

See the README for details and the source code.

action.description: Run the selected Java application or JUnit configuration with the scope-tracer agent and open the trace when it ends
